active_paradigms.idea: Replace the staged greedy hierarchy with a per-layer bottleneck MILP using scipy.optimize.milp
active_paradigms.description: The current program first greedily assigns fixed logical groups to nodes, then greedily allocates replicas independently inside each node, and finally greedily packs resulting copies onto GPUs. This is fast and preserves all cardinality constraints, but each irreversible stage optimizes a surrogate objective and cannot correct a poor earlier node/group decision. Formulate one per-layer mixed-integer bottleneck model whose binary variable assigns each physical GPU slot to a logical expert, with exactly the required number of slots per GPU and at least one copy for every expert. Add replica-count variables and a makespan variable T, enforcing that the traffic assigned to every GPU, computed as the sum of expert load divided by that expert's chosen replica count, is at most T. If hierarchical locality is required, forbid assignments outside the node selected for each group, or add an explicit group-to-node binary assignment with exact groups-per-node constraints. Use the current greedy result as an incumbent-derived upper bound on T and impose that bound before calling scipy.optimize.milp, so the solver only searches for an actual improvement. Use a small positive secondary objective on replica count imbalance or on traffic variance after minimizing T, rather than optimizing only an arbitrary expert ordering. This directly targets the likely evaluator bottleneck metric instead of separately balancing group totals, replica loads, and GPU totals.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary load-balance score: reduce the maximum physical-GPU load, especially cases where the current group-to-node partition strands a hot expert in an overloaded node. Use the greedy incumbent as a quality baseline and reject solver output unless its realized max load improves it.
active_paradigms.cautions: MILP can be too slow for large expert counts or many layers, so apply it only below a conservative size threshold and retain the current greedy algorithm as a timeout-safe fallback. The load contribution must use the final replica count, requiring standard binary-count linking variables or enumeration of allowable replica counts; a naive linear model that treats copy load as weight/count without linking is invalid. Preserve the evaluator's exact output invariants: every logical expert must have rank-0, ranks must be contiguous, every GPU must receive exactly num_replicas/num_gpus slots, and node restrictions must not be silently violated.

active_paradigms.idea: Use a one-shot Hungarian assignment repair to place fixed replicas into GPU slots
active_paradigms.description: Keep the current replica-count decision initially, but replace the final descending greedy physical-expert packing with a global slot assignment solved by scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment. Expand each GPU into its fixed number of physical-expert slots, and build a cost matrix between each replica copy and each allowable slot. Derive the cost from the greedy placement's leave-one-copy-out GPU load: for placing copy p of load a on GPU g, use a convex overload penalty such as max(0, base_load[g] + a - target)^2 plus a much smaller total-load penalty. Set an effectively infinite cost for slots on a different node, thereby retaining the current hierarchy and communication locality. One Hungarian call then jointly chooses all replica-to-GPU assignments within the cardinality constraints, unlike the current list/heap procedure whose early heavy placements are never reconsidered. Reconstruct physical-to-logical order and per-logical ranks from the selected slot assignment. This is particularly useful when many similarly heavy replicas exist: greedy LPT is good but can make avoidable tie-driven imbalances, while assignment gives a globally consistent repair under the chosen local linearization.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: GPU-level tail load and variance after replication, without changing the number of replicas or group/node allocation. This is a bounded-cost quality improvement over the current final packing stage and can improve score where imbalance is caused by placement rather than insufficient replication.
active_paradigms.cautions: The Hungarian cost is a linearized surrogate because true GPU load is coupled across all assigned copies; compute base_load by removing the source copy from its incumbent GPU to avoid charging it twice. Use a finite but safely dominant forbidden cost rather than infinity if the backend rejects infinities. Its cubic matrix cost can exceed greedy packing for large numbers of replicas, so gate it to small-to-medium per-node replica counts and compare the realized maximum load against the incumbent before accepting it.

active_paradigms.idea: Vectorize greedy replica allocation exactly through marginal-copy selection with torch.topk
active_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts loop performs one full max reduction over all logical experts for every redundant physical slot, which is costly when many extra replicas are available. Its selection rule has a useful exact characterization: allocating the k-th total copy of expert i is selected in descending order of the marginal next-copy load weight[i]/k, for k starting at 2. Build once the candidate tensor weight[:, :, None] divided by k=2 through num_redundant+1, flatten its expert-and-k dimensions, and select the num_redundant largest candidates per layer with torch.topk. Count selected candidates for each expert to obtain logcnt, then create phy2log and ranks in vectorized form from those counts. Because weight[i]/k is monotone decreasing in k, selecting top marginal values automatically satisfies the prefix property: no third copy can be selected without its second copy, apart from harmless equal-value tie choices. Thus the resulting replica counts minimize the same greedy water-filling criterion as the iterative routine, while eliminating repeated max/scatter updates and Python-level iteration. The saved execution time can be spent on a modest final placement refinement or directly improve any evaluator component that rewards rearrangement latency.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Algorithm execution time while preserving the current algorithm's replica-count quality exactly; it also makes behavior more deterministic by defining tie handling through a single top-k ordering. This addresses the efficiency half of the objective without risking a worse balance caused by a new heuristic.
active_paradigms.cautions: The candidate tensor has O(num_logical_experts * num_redundant) entries per layer, so only use it when this is smaller than the work and memory budget of repeated reductions; retain the existing loop for extremely large redundant counts. Floating-point ties can produce a different but equally balanced expert choice than heap/argmax, so ensure deterministic top-k behavior if evaluator reproducibility matters. Do not accidentally select k=1 candidates: every logical expert already has its mandatory original copy, and only k>=2 corresponds to a redundant slot.
